clue.text: Adulterous cavalier lax with two redheads at a time

indicators.note: a cavalier attitude is careless and offhand, so these letters are treated carelessly and rearranged

parts.note: the head of red is R, and two of them give a pair of Rs

explanation.surface: A loose-living rake who dates two redheaded women simultaneously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavalier' looks like a noun for the philanderer, but it signals that LAX, RR and ATATIME are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is sex outside wedlock, which is exactly what the longer adjective describes.

clue.text: Hollow story in every song that's designed for relaxation

indicators.note: the emptied story is placed inside the word for every

parts.note: every one means each

indicators.note: a hollow thing has no middle, so only the outside letters of story remain

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A tale told within each tune, written to help listeners unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair with deep cushions is a piece of furniture made for lounging and unwinding.

clue.text: Top features in magazine for British high-flyer

indicators.note: something that features in a publication appears inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: Time is the American news magazine
a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: A cover story in a magazine about a successful Briton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flyer' suggests a business star, but it is literal: the clue means the British astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: The British astronaut flew to the International Space Station in 2015, a literal high-flyer.

clue.text: A real giant for starters, the Guardian …

definitions.text: A real giant for starters, the Guardian …

indicators.note: starters are the opening courses, so each of the first three words gives its first letter

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself as we or us, so the Guardian is us

explanation.surface: Praise for a legendary figure at the newspaper, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: in Greek myth he was a hundred-eyed giant set to guard Io, so a giant guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-eyed giant of Greek myth was a watchman, and his name now means any vigilant guardian.

clue.text: … Guardian giant, artist, utterly charming, initially breaking into a song

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering it, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of utterly and charming are taken

explanation.surface: A tribute to a great of the paper, a charming artist bursting into song.
explanation.walkthrough: RA plus UC breaks into A ARIA, giving A + RAUC + ARIA. The famous Guardian setter took the name of the monkey-puzzle tree; the clue runs on from the previous one.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter John Graham, who used this pseudonym, was a towering figure among the newspaper's crossword compilers.

clue.text: One stands up as a Van Gogh painting

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to stand up is to rise, so stands up means rises

explanation.surface: Someone gets to their feet, much like a figure in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands up as' looks like a phrase about posing; it is a charade, with 'as' linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Gogh painted a famous canvas of blue flowers in the asylum garden at Saint-Rémy in 1889 under this title.

clue.text: A second taken by surprise

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: Someone startled for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' joins the pieces to the definition and completes the idiom: 'taken by surprise' is 'taken aback'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb appears in the idiom of being caught off guard, so it stands for suddenly and unexpectedly.

clue.text: Orb nicked from the famous Greek composer raised in European capital

indicators.note: nicked means stolen, so those letters are taken out of the name

parts.note: Zorba the Greek is the famous novel and film character

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is written upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A tale of a stolen orb and a Greek composer feted in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ORB from ZORBA leaves ZA; BERG upward gives GREB.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Croatia, a European country.

clue.text: Last of twelve, always standing in order

parts.note: December, DEC, is the last of the twelve months

indicators.note: standing up in a down entry means the word is written upwards

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A reference to the final item in a set of twelve kept permanently in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' is the poetic E'ER, which upward gives REE.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict or official ruling issued by an authority is an order.

clue.text: Since it needs milk, sort leaves for tea

parts.note: as can mean since, as in as it was raining
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the word for sort departs from milk

parts.note: ilk means sort or kind

explanation.surface: Advice that a variety of tea leaves is best taken with milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort leaves' looks like a description of tea leaves; it is ILK leaving MILK to give M. 'it' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention; 'needs' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The strong black variety grown in north-east India is a well-known kind of brew.

clue.text: Move towards Virginia holding that thing in jar

indicators.note: the rest is put inside the word for jar

parts.note: to jar is to grate, as on the nerves

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
it refers to that thing

explanation.surface: A traveller heads for Virginia carrying something in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a container noun but is the verb, to grate on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be drawn steadily towards something, as by gravity, is the sense of the verb.

clue.text: See 25
See 18 down
Old focus of a student's attention, daughter's after filthy swine

definitions.text: Old focus of a student's attention

indicators.note: the daughter is after, meaning placed after the rest

parts.note: filthy can mean black with dirt
a boar is a male swine

explanation.surface: A dirty pig trailed by a girl, oddly set beside a classroom scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Before whiteboards and screens, the teacher's writing surface at the front of the class held pupils' gaze.

clue.text: Essay under workbook for healthcare profession

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below the other letters

parts.note: work is OP (opus) and book is TOME
to essay is to try

explanation.surface: A written assignment set in a textbook for trainee health workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workbook' splits as work (OP) and book (TOME), with TRY below.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing eyesight and prescribing lenses is a branch of health care practised by opticians.

clue.text: Ace in hearts, possibly, a king (diamonds) — and queen, perhaps?

indicators.note: the first word goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Hearts (Heart of Midlothian) is an Edinburgh football club, FC
R stands for rex, Latin for king
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in ... notation

explanation.surface: A run through a hand of playing cards: ace, king and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' looks like the card suit, but it is Hearts (Heart of Midlothian), an Edinburgh football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are the picture cards in a pack, so a queen is one example.

clue.text: Engineer casual with tie loose

indicators.note: loose means let free and untied, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An engineer dressed down, with a relaxed tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a person; it is the verb, to bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to make it happen, which is to make it real.

clue.text: Knight abducted by prince, soldier unaware

indicators.note: something abducted is held captive, so it goes inside the captor

parts.note: Prince Igor is the hero of Borodin's opera
N is the chess notation for a knight
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A knight is kidnapped by a prince while a soldier knows nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge of something means being uninformed about it.

clue.text: See 15
Old singer-songwriter caught private detective hired by wife?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a wife suspicious of her husband might hire someone to check up on her hubby

explanation.surface: A suspicious wife hires an investigator, and an old pop star gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented description of a husband-checker. The answer is the American singer behind 'The Twist'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American performer of 'The Twist' was a rock and roll star of the early 1960s, hence 'Old'.

clue.text: Hand in the air, it's true!

parts.note: a straight is a poker hand of five cards in sequence
up means aloft, in the air

explanation.surface: Someone raises a hand to swear they are telling the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand in the air' looks like one phrase for a raised arm; 'Hand' is the poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal slang for honestly, used to insist that one is not lying.

clue.text: European resembling pond life, if a tad over the top?

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece over the top sits above the rest, so the answer is what is left when that top piece is removed

parts.note: a made-up adjective for being like a tadpole, a creature of ponds
the clue words a tad, spelt TAD

explanation.surface: A mocking remark that someone from Europe looks rather like pond life.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke works backwards: put TAD over the top of the answer and you get a word meaning tadpole-like; 'if' joins the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for people and things from Poland, a European country, is also a noun for its language.

clue.text: Is man one, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A question about whether humans count as apes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: asking whether man is an ape-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to apes and monkeys, and humans are primates closely related to them.

clue.text: Metal content of mug or cup, perhaps?

definitions.text: Metal content of mug or cup, perhaps?

parts.words: Metal content of mug or cup, perhaps?
parts.note: the middle letter of mug, and of cup, is U, the chemical symbol of a radioactive metal

explanation.surface: A query about what metal a drinking vessel is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' is not what the vessel holds or is made of: it is the letter inside each word, U, which is the element's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The radioactive element with atomic number 92 has the chemical symbol U, the inside letter of both words.

clue.text: Sound car going over circuit

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means placed above the following letter

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
a circuit is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A car making a lap of a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: The word refers to recorded or transmitted sound, as opposed to the picture.

clue.text: Wise guy, king with open access?

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
open access suggests there is no barrier, no wall

explanation.surface: A smart monarch who lets everyone in.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise guy is a smart alec who claims to understand everything.

clue.text: Sort of dark, in darkest passage

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch of text, so the answer is a stretch running through these words

explanation.surface: A description of a gloomy, very dark corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' looks like a dark corridor; it signals a run of letters across 'darK IN DArkest'.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal contraction of kind of means rather or somewhat, the same as sort of.

clue.text: They're taken to court (commercial name in China)?

indicators.note: the bracketed words are placed in the brackets that the clue prints around them

parts.note: the closing bracket stands for the brackets around the phrase; china is porcelain, of which Minton is a maker
a commercial is an advertisement, AD
Minton is a famous name in china, the English porcelain maker

explanation.surface: Criminal schemes prosecuted in court, with a hint about a Chinese trade name.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own punctuation is wordplay: what is written in brackets sits inside the word BRACKETS. 'China' looks like the country but means porcelain, where Minton is a famous name.
explanation.definitionFit: Players carry these lightweight strung bats onto a court to hit a shuttlecock over the net.

clue.text: Author, possibly K or M — S is wrong

parts.note: Kingsley and Martin Amis, father and son, are both English novelists

explanation.surface: A complaint that one letter in a list of initials is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: K and M stand for Kingsley and Martin, two writers sharing a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone awry or out of order is described by this adverb or adjective.

clue.text: Exuberant man jumped on plaything

parts.note: an exuberant person is full of bounce
a castle (rook) is one of the men in chess

explanation.surface: A lively fellow leapt onto a toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' looks like a person; it is a chess piece, the rook.
explanation.definitionFit: Children leap about on the inflatable structure at fairs and parties, so it is a toy for jumping on.
